name: ReachStream
summary: B2B contact database with a published price instead of a quote: unlimited contact and company views on every tier, with the meter running on exports rather than on looking. Annual billing takes 20% off the price and changes nothing about the allowance. Read on their own pricing page, re-read 12 November 2026.
best_for: small sales and marketing teams that want a B2B contact database with a published price rather than a quote, and whose volume is predictable enough to size in exports a month: the tier below the ones where ZoomInfo and Cognism start.
skip_if: you need more than three seats without an enterprise conversation; your volume is spiky, because nothing on the page tells you what an extra credit costs; or your market is outside the sectors where their data is strongest, in which case ask for a sample against your own ICP before you pay.
honest_knock: The meter is on exporting, not on looking, and that is the number to size before you pick a tier. Contact and company views are unlimited on every plan including the free one, so the demo will feel generous; what you actually pay for is pulling those records out, and separately for revealing an email address, which is a second meter the plan cards do not put next to the first. Free gives 100 exports and 200 email views a month, which is a sample rather than a workflow. The second thing to check is seats: Starter and Pro both include exactly one, so a two-person sales team is on Business at $99 a month before it needs the extra credits. Credits do not roll over: the FAQ, re-read on 12 November 2026, says unused credits reset at the start of each new billing cycle, so a plan sized for a busy month is simply wasted in a quiet one. That same question answered the other way on 10 September, which is reason enough to check it yourself before you commit. Underbuying is no clearer either: two figures on the page are not explained anywhere: Starter and Pro promise to "unlock an extra $250 / $500 worth of data", which is priced in dollars rather than in credits or records, and the cost of a credit once you run out is not published at all.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-10 in a browser on reachstream.com/prospect/pricing/ with both billing toggles, and re-verified against that same page on 19 September 2026 -- every amount, credit allowance and seat count below is unchanged; only the credit-rollover answer in the FAQ has flipped) Five tiers in USD. Free is $0 with 100 export credits and 200 email views a month (1,200 and 2,400 a year). Starter is $39 a month, or $29 on annual billing, for 5,000 export credits a month (60,000 a year). Pro is $59 or $49 for 10,000 a month. Business is $99 or $79 for 20,000 a month (240,000 a year) and, for the first time, up to three seats instead of one. Enterprise is quote-only. The annual discount is a flat 20% on the price and nothing else: the credit allowance is identical either way. Two meters run separately — export credits are spent downloading to CSV or syncing to a CRM, email credits are spent revealing an address in the platform or the Chrome extension — while contact and company insight views are unlimited on every tier including Free. Email views are unlimited on all paid tiers. The FAQ, re-read on 19 September 2026, states that unused credits do not roll over and that they reset at the start of each new billing cycle -- on 10 September that same question answered the other way round, so size the plan for an ordinary month rather than a busy one and confirm the rule before you buy. It also states that direct-dial and mobile numbers are included on Starter, Pro and Business. Note that the main /pricing/ page carries no figures at all — it only routes you to Prospect or Email Verifier — and that the site answers a plain HTTP request with 403, so the figures above come from a browser reading of the Prospect pricing page one level down.

compare_with.name: RocketReach
compare_with.why: RocketReach sells the same shape of thing, a contact database with self-serve tiers, and both publish their prices, which already puts them in a different bracket from the quote-only end of this market. The difference is what the meter counts. ReachStream meters exports and leaves views unlimited, so the question is how many records you pull; RocketReach meters lookups, so the question is how often you search. If your team browses widely and exports rarely, ReachStream is the cheaper shape. If you export in bulk from a narrow list, check the per-record maths on both before assuming the lower headline price wins

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested ReachStream on the Free plan: one AI company search and one company profile. No contacts were viewed or exported. Prospect search, tab Companies, AI Search with the query Software companies in the Netherlands with 50 to 200 employees returned after about 8 seconds Search Results: 205 Companies with 1,333 Contacts. The columns are Company Name, Website, Employees, Annual Revenue, Actions (Quick View, download) and Company Location, and the Industry filter was set to Technology automatically. Rows seen first: 2getthere (Utrecht, 50 to 100 employees, 10M to 25M dollars revenue), 2solar By Sollit, 4dotnet, 50five, Acico Yachts, Adapta and Advcash. Quality was mixed: not every result is a software company; 2getthere is listed as Urban Transit Services and Acico Yachts was noted as not a software company. Quick View of the company 2getthere shows a description, website, LinkedIn link and location, with the buttons Add to List and download. Credits afterwards: download 0 of 100, view 0 of 200 and AI search 1 of 2. Opening a company profile cost nothing and the AI search cost 1 of 2. No contact was viewed or exported, so the quality of contact data, the accuracy of verified emails and the credit use per export are not tested. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Onboarding takes 4 screens with every field required before the Prospect Hub opens, and the AI search matched size and country better than the software sector. Free allows only 2 AI searches.

sessions.what: We ran one AI company search in ReachStream's Prospect Hub on the Free plan on 13 November 2026 and read the credits and plans screens. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We viewed and exported no contacts. We did not test the data quality of contacts, checkout, support or cancellation.
findings: Setup was a four-screen window asking for company, role, biggest challenge, contacts per month and how we heard of ReachStream. All fields were required and no card was asked for. The home screen showed the Free plan with 100 downloads, 200 views and 2 AI searches in the account credits.

We searched in plain English for software companies in the Netherlands with 50 to 200 employees. After about eight seconds it returned 205 companies with 1,333 contacts. The search used 1 of the 2 AI search credits.
Quality was mixed. At least two results were not software firms: one is a transit services company and one builds yachts.
Opening a company profile with Quick View used no credits. We did not open any contact.

The upgrade window preselects yearly payment at 20% off. Free lists 1,200 export credits a year, Starter $29 a month billed annually with 60,000, Pro $49 with 120,000 and Business $79 with 240,000 and three seats. Free, Starter and Pro include one seat. The app does not say whether unused credits carry over, and we did not test that.
not_tested: Sign-up on a fresh account (we joined an existing one)
Contact data quality, email accuracy and credits spent per export
Checkout, support, invitations, roles, API, export and cancelling
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
